clue.text: Citadel's fallen in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: a citadel that has fallen is knocked down and in ruins, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter; the word itself is the fodder

explanation.surface: A fortress has fallen, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like a throwaway phrase, but 'manner of speaking' is the definition and 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional variety of a language is a particular way people talk.

clue.text: Intractable problem of upsetting cover to Austen novel

indicators.note: upsetting turns the word over, so in a down clue it reads upwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is a novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: The tricky question of overturning a book cover on a Jane Austen novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' reverses LID to DIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a quandary where every choice seems bad.

clue.text: Relate to a forward engulfed by anguish

indicators.note: the cheeky word is swallowed up inside the word for anguish

parts.note: pain is anguish
forward, of a person, means cheeky or pert

explanation.surface: Connecting with a pushy player swamped by distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' looks like a sports position but means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: To belong or pertain to something is to have a connection with it.

clue.text: Medical fluid used in gene mapping

indicators.note: the answer is found used inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A fluid deployed in genetic research.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid injected into the rectum to clear the bowels is a medical treatment.

clue.text: Defeat by moving wildly

explanation.surface: Losing heavily by flailing about.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy beating in a contest, and also flailing or tossing violently about.

clue.text: Creepy club containing weird bar

indicators.note: the club wraps around the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon

indicators.note: weird suggests something bent out of its usual shape, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A spooky nightclub that houses a strange bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' turns BAR into ABR, which 'containing' puts inside MACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something gruesome that makes the flesh crawl.

clue.text: Man doesn't have time to be a niggard

indicators.note: the word loses a letter, since it no longer has it

parts.note: mister is the title for a man

explanation.surface: A man who has no time to be stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinflint who hoards money is stingy.

clue.text: Enclosed in hold of craft

indicators.note: in signals the shut-in word goes inside the word for hold

parts.note: to carry is to hold
pent means penned or shut in

explanation.surface: Locked in the hold of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a boat, but it is a skill, woodworking.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodworking is a skilled trade.

clue.text: Convey with BO?

parts.note: the letter B accompanied by an O, a letter shaped like a ring, read as a picture of letters

explanation.surface: Is body odour a thing to carry around?
explanation.walkthrough: BO usually means body odour; here it is pictured as B with an O beside it, and O is ring-shaped, so B plus RING.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry or fetch something along is to convey it.

clue.text: Hartnell's unfinished design for entrance

indicators.note: design signals the letters are reshaped into a new pattern
unfinished means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Norman Hartnell was a British fashion designer; the 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: An incomplete dress by a fashion designer, created for a grand entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: Hartnell was the British couturier who dressed the Queen. 'unfinished' drops the final L, and 'design' rearranges HARTNEL. 'entrance' is the verb (en-TRANCE), not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate or spellbind someone is to entrance them.

clue.text: Gradual decline due to drinks and drug

parts.note: a cat drinks by lapping, so drinks can mean laps
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone sliding downhill because of booze and pills.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling-off in standards or a slide into a worse state is a slow slipping back.

clue.text: Practice lines to remain in control

indicators.note: one thing lines another when it sits inside it as a lining, so these letters go within

parts.note: to rest can mean to remain, as in 'let it rest there'
to practise is to train

explanation.surface: Rehearsing your script so you keep your composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' looks like an actor's script, but it is the container signal: TRAIN forms the lining of REST. 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-control and holding back are the same quality of keeping oneself in check.

clue.text: Combine with answer that's included "duck"

indicators.note: the abbreviation for answer is placed inside the word for a business combination

parts.note: a combine is a business group, the kind formed by a merger

explanation.surface: An instruction to merge with an answer that contains the word duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combine' reads as a verb but is the noun for a business group.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a species of fish-eating diving bird of the waterfowl family.

clue.text: Desiring bet with leader in opposition

indicators.note: the leading letter, a compass point, is swapped for the point opposite it

parts.note: a wager is a bet

explanation.surface: Wanting to place a bet against the party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: W (west) at the front of WAGER is replaced by its opposite compass point, E (east). 'leader in opposition' looks political.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and longing for something both describe strong wanting.

clue.text: Prize is a pullover?

parts.note: split as pull (draw) plus over, which turns draw the other way round

explanation.surface: Is a woolly jumper the prize?
explanation.walkthrough: 'pullover' looks like a sweater but splits into 'pull' (DRAW) and 'over', which reverses it to WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy or honour given to a winner is a prize.

clue.text: I lied having spoken about turning up for analytical opinion

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the built word from bottom to top
the word for spoken goes around the other letters

parts.note: said means spoken
a lied is a German art song

explanation.surface: Someone lied, then went back on what they said, about their findings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lied' looks like a lie but is the German word for a song. SAID 'about' I SONG gives SISONGAID, and 'turning up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's identification of an illness is a considered judgement from analysis.

clue.text: The same arrangement as in 1 across

indicators.note: an arrangement is a new ordering of the letters given

parts.note: the cross-reference points to the solution of 1 across, a way of speaking

explanation.surface: Arranged exactly as in a previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The solution of 1 across (DIALECT) plus IN are rearranged ('arrangement').
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that are exactly alike match in every respect.

clue.text: Elite were mounted by conductor

parts.note: the elect are a chosen elite
rode means travelled mounted on a horse

explanation.surface: The elite were outdone by a bandleader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' looks like an orchestra leader but is an electrical conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal through which electricity passes is a conductor of current.

clue.text: Lizard is animal that absorbs hydrogen over a long period

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece
the animal takes in the symbol, holding it inside

parts.note: a camel is an animal
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
an eon is a very long period of time

explanation.surface: A lizard is a beast that soaks up gas over ages.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' puts the CHAMEL above EON.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a colour-changing reptile from Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Confined to fish for mullet

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means shut in
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Something shut away for fishing for a mullet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mullet' looks like the fish, but in heraldry a mullet is a five-pointed star.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a mullet is a star of five points, the same figure as a five-pointed star outline.

clue.text: Religious mischief-maker in dugout

parts.note: pi is slang for pious or religious
a rogue is a rascal or mischief-maker

explanation.surface: A pious troublemaker hiding in a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dugout' looks like a trench or a sports shelter but here is a canoe hollowed from a log.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe carved out of a single tree trunk is a dugout.

clue.text: Long period of time to end of season

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A long stretch of time until the season finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective but is the verb, meaning to pine.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine or crave for something is to have a strong wish.

clue.text: Point to inclination that's developing

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass
an ascent is an upward slope or inclination

explanation.surface: Pointing to a slope that is forming.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just coming into being and beginning to grow is emerging.

clue.text: Paddy's said to have this poison

indicators.note: said tells us the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: a paddy field has rice in it, so what a paddy has is rice in

explanation.surface: An Irishman is reputed to keep this toxin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irishman but is a flooded rice field; 'rice in' said aloud gives the toxin's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a deadly toxin extracted from castor-oil beans.

clue.text: Third arm to go up

parts.note: C is the third letter of the alphabet
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A third arm to help you ascend.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascending is moving upward.

clue.text: Not having a tie that can't be worsted

explanation.surface: Being tieless and unbeatable.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally lacking a match or equal, and so unbeatable or peerless.

clue.text: Butch lady's beginning to divide the majority

indicators.note: the letter splits the other word, sitting within it

parts.note: the many means the majority of people

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tough woman starts to split the majority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lady's beginning' is L, which goes between MAN and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Butch describes a tough, masculine manner.

clue.text: Custom's bit of a laugh?

indicators.note: bit of a laugh reads as the bit belonging to the laugh, so it follows it

parts.note: ha is a laugh
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is the tradition just a joke?
explanation.definitionFit: A regular practice or established way of doing something is a custom.

clue.text: Islands go to make a rippling effect

indicators.note: the fodder letters are used to make a new word, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Islands going to create ripples.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, a rapid slide up or down the scale sounds like a ripple of notes.

clue.text: Old note about English part of speech

indicators.note: about indicates the word for a part of speech turns round

parts.note: a verb is one of the parts of speech

explanation.surface: An old note about a piece of English grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses VERB to BREV.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, this is a long note value now seldom used, worth two semibreves.

clue.text: Shortened them by taking fool on official mission

parts.note: 'em is a clipped form of them

indicators.note: the letters of by take in the word for fool, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A shortened party who took a fool on an official visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegation of envoys sent abroad on state business is a diplomatic mission.

clue.text: Start of written work included coming back from dead

annotationWithheld.why: Start of written work included coming back from dead: EXTINCT seems to be TEXT with its first letter moved to the back plus INC, but 'included' would have to give INC and also be the container indicator; no separate signal is found.
